title: Cahn's 1969 recordings and documentary of the White Eagles
summary: A recording of the White Eagles is played; Cahn says he filmed a 30-minute documentary in 1969 following the tribes from New Year's to St. Joseph's Day.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You've done some recording of the Indian tribes of Mardi Gras. And this is how some of them sound. Let's see if we can get this machine going. We'll have to wait a little while. Let's see. The machine was not turned on. We just turned the machine on. Let it warm up. It's 12 minutes after 9 o'clock. And let's see if we can get it going right now. Fireball! Fireball!

Let's go. Fireball! 된 된 된 된 된  We'll be right back. We'll be right back. We'll be right back. My flag is rally. My flag is rally. They make no humba. They sing everybody. They sing everybody.
Jules, what tribe was this? And when was this? White Eagles. Okay. This was the White Eagle Band? When was this done?

The White Eagle Tribe. They don't have a band. This was done in 1969. That's the time I did a documentary for myself and followed the Indians from the 1st of January on through Mardi Gras Day and then followed them on into St. Joseph Day on film.
Right. You did shoot a documentary, you said, on the Indians.
Yes, sure. It's approximately a 30-minute documentary on the Indians.
